daedf173a6:18521666d83e4a8f.summary: Following a three-week trial, a federal jury in Cleveland convicted three members of the Fully Blooded Felons, a violent Cleveland street gang, of a number of crimes, including Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations (RICO) Act murder, RICO conspiracy, RICO kidnapping, drug trafficking, and gun crimes.

daedf173a6:cb25ff7e632443ca.title: U.S. Trustee Program Prevails at Trial to Revoke $3.9M Discharge from Seattle Man Who Concealed Inheritance Rights and Business Interest
daedf173a6:cb25ff7e632443ca.summary: A Seattle man who concealed an inheritance and his interest in a business lost his bankruptcy discharge of more than $3.9 million after a trial victory by the Justice Department’s U.S. Trustee Program (USTP).

daedf173a6:2dd969bd3a1464a3.title: Department of Justice Launches Super Intelligence Task Force
daedf173a6:2dd969bd3a1464a3.summary: The U.S. Department of Justice is announcing the formation of its Super Intelligence (SI) Task Force (DOJ-SITF). President Trump has made clear that “America stands at the forefront of a new technological revolution in intelligence,” and the Department will be a leader in safeguarding against malicious SI actors.

daedf173a6:ba922de121eea7ea.title: Los Angeles Woman Charged for $18M COVID-19 Relief Fraud Scheme
daedf173a6:ba922de121eea7ea.summary: A federal grand jury in the Central District of California returned an indictment yesterday charging Marisela Nuno, 53, of Los Angeles, California, with an $18 million scheme to defraud the Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) and the Economic Injury Disaster Loan (EIDL) program, federal stimulus programs authorized as part of the Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security (CARES) Act.

daedf173a6:56f31da86da435de.title: Attorney General Blanche, Governor Landry, Senator Cassidy, and Louisiana Officials Announce East Baton Rouge Parish as Winner of the Model Cities Initiative

daedf173a6:2a53591c0a7847f1.title: Utah Minor Recovered by Law Enforcement After Oregon Man Allegedly Transported the Victim to Engage in Criminal Sexual Activity
daedf173a6:2a53591c0a7847f1.summary: An Oregon man is now in federal custody and charged in a criminal complaint with transportation with intent to engage in criminal sexual activity after he allegedly met a Utah minor online in May 2025, drove to Utah to pick up the victim, and then transported the victim to his residence across state lines.

daedf173a6:a8338fb5ea5f29bb.title: DOJ To Monitor Elections in All 50 States for First Time
daedf173a6:a8338fb5ea5f29bb.summary: One of the Department of Justice’s (DOJ) most important missions is ensuring election integrity, supporting free and fair elections, and protecting the right to vote for U.S. citizens across the United States. The DOJ has sent election monitors in support of this mission since the enactment of the Voting Rights Act in 1965 across all Administrations.

daedf173a6:571a6f54def6e329.title: Oklahoma Man Charged in Connection with Sending Threatening Letters Containing Non-Toxic White Powder to Election and Government Officials Across the Country
daedf173a6:571a6f54def6e329.summary: Robin Patrick Martin, 67, of Oklahoma City, has been charged with conveying false or misleading information and hoaxes and mailing threatening communications in connection with threatening letters mailed to state election officials, members of Congress, the FBI and others.

daedf173a6:e84db2cc3fed10cf.title: Former U.S. Government Contractor Pleads Guilty to Spying for Ethiopia
daedf173a6:e84db2cc3fed10cf.summary: Abraham Teklu Lemma, 53, of Maryland, a former information technology contractor at the National Reconnaissance Office, the U.S. Department of State, and the U.S. Department of Justice pleaded guilty today to conspiring to commit espionage on behalf of the government of the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia.

daedf173a6:42cdea27dcac3255.title: Defense and Aerospace Contractors ILC Dover and ILC Astrospace Agree to Pay $13M to Resolve Cybersecurity Fraud Allegations
daedf173a6:42cdea27dcac3255.summary: Defense and aerospace companies ILC Dover LP and ILC Astrospace LLC, of Frederica, Delaware, have agreed to pay $13 million to resolve allegations that they violated the False Claims Act by failing to comply with cybersecurity requirements in their contracts with the Department of the Army, the Missile Defense Agency, and the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA).

daedf173a6:f82aaeb41b6a7a38.title: Ohio Pet Breeder Agrees to Surrender Over 1,100 Chinchillas
daedf173a6:f82aaeb41b6a7a38.summary: The U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Ohio endorsed a consent decree entered between the United States and the owner of R & R Chinchilla Inc. to surrender over 300 remaining chinchillas at a breeding facility in Jenera, Ohio. The court order follows R & R Chinchilla’s voluntary surrender of roughly 800 additional chinchillas to animal welfare organizations pursuant to a modified temporary restraining order.

daedf173a6:6af5aa394bb55d76.title: American Man Extradited from Germany to Face Charges of Defrauding U.S. Consumers in Fake Psychic Mailing-Fraud Scheme
daedf173a6:6af5aa394bb55d76.summary: Mael Chemla, 61, a U.S., French, and Israeli national, previously residing in Aventura, Florida, was extradited to the United States from Germany and made his initial appearance in Miami federal court yesterday to face charges for his role in operating a mailing fraud scheme.

daedf173a6:21f1d33ada86bec9.title: Lockheed Martin Agrees to Pay $29.5M to Resolve Alleged Employment Discrimination Violations
daedf173a6:21f1d33ada86bec9.summary: Today, the U.S. Department of Justice and the U.S. Equal Employment Commission (EEOC) announced a two-part settlement against Lockheed Martin Corporation, headquartered in Bethesda, Maryland. Lockheed has agreed to pay a total of approximately $29.5 million to resolve allegations relating to employment discrimination and related false certifications of compliance with federal civil rights laws while serving as a federal contractor. This includes $22 million to be paid to the United States pursuant to an agreement with the Justice Department to resolve allegations that Lockheed violated the False Claims Act arising from failures to comply with anti-discrimination requirements in its federal contracts and by discriminating against employees and applicants on the basis of their race or sex. It also includes approximately $7.5 million to be paid to over 1,000 affected Lockheed employees pursuant to a negotiated settlement agreement with the EEOC resolving a 2025 Commissioner’s Charge filed by EEOC Chair Andrea Lucas, which alleged Lockheed violated Title VII of the Civil Rights Act by engaging in race discrimination against white employees, including in performance assessments and in bonus and other compensation decisions. This is the largest class of workers to publicly recover under an EEOC settlement on account of alleged Title VII violations arising from or relating to a DEI program or practices.

daedf173a6:8a775e25fc416bdb.title: Justice Department Announces Charges Involving 63 Individuals for Election-Related Crimes
daedf173a6:8a775e25fc416bdb.summary: Today, the Justice Department announced charges involving 63 individuals, including four illegal aliens, in connection with illegal voting, fraudulent voter registration, and related election crimes across the country. The cases include voting by aliens in federal elections, false claims of U.S. citizenship to register to vote or to vote, and the fraudulent submission of a voter registration application in another state.

daedf173a6:1aa5c8ee71463842.title: Former BizJet Sales Manager Pleads Guilty to Foreign Bribery
daedf173a6:1aa5c8ee71463842.summary: Jald Jensen, 73, of Panama City, and previously of Van Nuys, California, a former sales manager of BizJet International Sales and Support Inc. (BizJet), pleaded guilty today for his role in connection with a scheme to pay bribes to government officials in Latin America to secure business for BizJet.

daedf173a6:bc260bb4feb6f45c.title: Justice Department Announces Nearly $300 Million in Awards to Four Model Cities to Combat Violent Crime and Restore Law and Order
daedf173a6:bc260bb4feb6f45c.summary: Today, the Justice Department announced the selection of four jurisdictions to receive nearly $300 million in federal funding through its Model Cities Initiative (MCI), a flagship effort to reduce violent crime, restore law and order, and strengthen public safety in American communities.

daedf173a6:5cd2aefe3c5c2214.title: Justice Department Announces Issuance of Federal Registrations for Medical Marijuana Dispensaries
daedf173a6:5cd2aefe3c5c2214.summary: The U.S. Department of Justice today announced that the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) is moving forward with the initial issuance of hundreds of federal registrations to qualifying state-licensed medical marijuana dispensaries under the Attorney General’s order implementing Schedule III controls for certain medical marijuana activities.

daedf173a6:80f44bf7cf316bd7.title: Justice Department Defends the Navy’s Actions to Address a Fuel Release at Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam in Hawaii
daedf173a6:80f44bf7cf316bd7.summary: The U.S. District Court for the District of Hawaii earlier this week ruled that the U.S. Navy is not in violation of the Clean Water Act after it reviewed the Navy’s response to fuel releases in 2020 and 2021 at Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam on Oahu, Hawaii, and other substantial improvements the Navy has made in the fueling infrastructure and operations. The ruling follows a bench trial that was held earlier this year regarding claims that the Navy is in violation of the Clean Water Act at the Joint Base.

daedf173a6:ce2d5a9137ab896b.title: Former Correctional Officer Sentenced on Federal Civil Rights Charges in Connection with Conspiracy to Violate Inmates’ Rights at West Virginia Jail
daedf173a6:ce2d5a9137ab896b.summary: A former correctional officer from the Southern Regional Jail in Beaver, West Virginia, was sentenced today to 24 months in prison for his role in a conspiracy in which he and other correctional officers used unreasonable and unjustified force against inmates, including pretrial detainees, as a form of punishment and retaliation. Michael Pack, 40, pleaded guilty on March 30 before U.S. Magistrate Judge Omar J. Aboulhosn to one count of violating 18 U.S.C. § 371.

daedf173a6:f4458245fc7dc056.title: Former U.S. Government Contractor Arrested for Allegedly Leaking National Defense Information and Stealing Night Vision Goggles
daedf173a6:f4458245fc7dc056.summary: James Thomas Ashbacher, 37, of Spring Lake, North Carolina, a former U.S. government contractor, was arrested by the FBI on Tuesday for allegedly leaking national defense information by posting the information on a popular social media site, unlawfully retaining other national defense information at his residence, and stealing night vision goggles from the U.S. Army’s Special Operations Command.

daedf173a6:9cb363e0f45f89cc.title: Florida Pharmacist Sentenced to Over 7 Years in Prison for Massive Illegal Oxycodone Distribution Conspiracy
daedf173a6:9cb363e0f45f89cc.summary: A Florida pharmacist and pharmacy owner was sentenced yesterday to 90 months in prison for her role in illegally dispensing over 300,000 oxycodone 30mg pills to pharmacy patrons who had no medical need for the drug.

daedf173a6:16ff12f335848fb9.title: Botox Fraud Doctor Sentenced to 15 Years in Prison for $45M Medicare Scheme
daedf173a6:16ff12f335848fb9.summary: California doctor Violetta Mailyan was sentenced yesterday to 15 years in prison for using her medical practice to fraudulently bill Medicare more than $45 million for Botox injection services that were medically unnecessary and never provided.

daedf173a6:7fc7abc3ca3e3d4c.title: Justice Department’s Statement on Its Investigation of Vistra’s Acquisition of Cogentrix
daedf173a6:7fc7abc3ca3e3d4c.summary: Associate Attorney General Stanley E. Woodward, Jr. of the U.S. Department of Justice issued the following statement today in connection with the Antitrust Division’s investigation into the acquisition of Cogentrix Energy (Cogentrix) by Vistra Corp. (Vistra) (together, the “Parties”):

daedf173a6:65eace906c859b19.title: Justice Department Announces Final Rule Allowing Federal Firearms Licensees to Voluntarily Use NICS for Employee Background Checks
daedf173a6:65eace906c859b19.summary: Today, the Department of Justice announced a final rule authorizing Federal Firearms Licensees (FFLs) to voluntarily use the FBI's National Instant Criminal Background Check System (NICS) to conduct background checks on certain current and prospective employees.

daedf173a6:8d9a06777c5e0159.title: Two Men Sentenced for Acting as Agents of the People’s Republic of China

daedf173a6:4fd5e98a2b7ea624.title: Indian National Pleads Guilty to $227M Medicare Fraud
daedf173a6:4fd5e98a2b7ea624.summary: An Indian national pleaded guilty today to a $227 million Medicare fraud scheme in which hundreds of thousands of Medicare beneficiaries’ personally identifiable information was purchased from a company based in Pakistan and used to bill Medicare for COVID-19 test kits that were never provided.

daedf173a6:fefe0390f71f9d2c.title: Israeli National Extradited to Face Charges for Stealing Nearly $3M in Virtual Currency Heist
daedf173a6:fefe0390f71f9d2c.summary: Alexander Gurevich, 49, an Israeli national, had his initial appearance today in the Northern District of California on a 2023 indictment that charged him for exploiting the Nomad Bridge’s self-executing computer program, also known as a smart contract, to steal $2.89 million in virtual currency.

daedf173a6:114baef691036615.title: California Man Pleads Guilty to Attempting to Provide Material Support to the Islamic State of Iraq and al-Sham
daedf173a6:114baef691036615.summary: Ammaad Akhtar, 34, of California, pleaded guilty today to attempting to provide material support to a designated foreign terrorist organization.

daedf173a6:a70cade41d4254b2.title: DOJ’s Fraud Division and the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District Minnesota Uncover Nearly $30M in Benefits Fraud in Enforcement Surge
daedf173a6:a70cade41d4254b2.summary: The Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division (Fraud Division), and the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Minnesota announced a series of enforcement actions targeting fraud involving taxpayer-funded Medicaid and SNAP programs.

daedf173a6:9f9d378e1798fb05.title: Justice Department Announces New Director of the U.S. Trustee Program
daedf173a6:9f9d378e1798fb05.summary: The Justice Department announced today that Attorney General Todd Blanche has selected Stephen V. Falanga to serve as Director of the U.S. Trustee Program (USTP) effective November 2.

daedf173a6:6e4bea6ffd70ba77.title: DOJ Announces Significant Charges Related to Ghost Student Fraud

daedf173a6:eccda5d36f2bb773.title: Man Pleads Guilty to Federal Hate Crimes in Deadly Attack on Boulder, Colorado, Gathering
daedf173a6:eccda5d36f2bb773.summary: Mohamed Sabry Soliman, 46, of Colorado Springs, Colorado, pleaded guilty in federal court today to 12 hate crimes charges for using Molotov cocktails to attack members of the group Run for Their Lives and others.

daedf173a6:7e93d28c856aab02.title: Former U.S. Postal Service Official Pleads Guilty to Bribery Scheme Related to Contracts Worth Hundreds of Millions of Dollars
daedf173a6:7e93d28c856aab02.summary: James E. Lee Sr., a former procurement official for the U.S. Postal Service, pleaded guilty today to conspiring to commit bribery and honest services wire fraud.

daedf173a6:a807c0b44d55ff94.title: Justice Department Unveils Indictments in Nationwide ‘Ghost Student’ Fraud Scam Linked to Kenyan Network
daedf173a6:a807c0b44d55ff94.summary: The Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division (Fraud Division), along with the U.S. Attorney’s Offices for the Eastern District of Virginia, Nebraska, and New Jersey announced indictments resulting from Operation Ghostbusters . Operation Ghostbusters is a nationwide investigation into a large‑scale student‑loan fraud scheme in which criminal actors created fraudulent Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) accounts using stolen U.S. citizen identities to enroll “ghost students” in educational institutions. After loan and grant disbursements, the refunds were diverted to bank accounts controlled by foreign actors and facilitated by U.S.-based money mules, including Kenyan nationals.

daedf173a6:70fd7df7253b0114.title: U.S. Extradites to El Salvador Southern California Man to Face Charges of Murdering Woman in Front of Infant Son, Whom He Abandoned
daedf173a6:70fd7df7253b0114.summary: A dual U.S.-Salvadoran citizen and Riverside County, California man has been extradited at the request of the Government of El Salvador so that he may face trial for allegedly murdering a woman in front of their toddler son in 2019, then abandoning the boy, whom farm workers found several days later, severely dehydrated, hungry and showing signs of child abuse.

daedf173a6:cb445e2c20720152.title: Justice Department Charges 18 More in North Carolina with Illegally Voting in 2024 Election
daedf173a6:cb445e2c20720152.summary: Today, the Justice Department announced that 18 aliens, including an illegal alien, in North Carolina have been indicted for illegally voting. Nine were charged in the Eastern District of North Carolina, five were charged in the Middle District of North Carolina, and four were charged in the Western District of North Carolina. These indictments are in addition to 12 individuals who were previously indicted in the Eastern District of North Carolina for illegally voting, bringing the statewide total to 30 indicted this year.

daedf173a6:f760ee76e25f4133.title: Justice Department Provides Update on Collaboration with State Attorneys General on Review of Local Mergers
daedf173a6:f760ee76e25f4133.summary: The Department of Justice provided the following update on the Antitrust Division’s collaboration with state Attorneys General regarding investigations of mergers with predominantly intrastate effects.

daedf173a6:d911d7236dc87ad8.title: Antitrust Division Announces Successful Referrals in Two Local Asphalt Merger Investigations to State Attorneys General
daedf173a6:d911d7236dc87ad8.summary: The Justice Department’s Antitrust Division provided the following statement on the closing of its investigations into two transactions that presented competition issues in local asphalt markets: (1) the acquisition of Suit-Kote Corporation by Colas Inc., a subsidiary of Bouygues S.A.; and (2) the acquisition of Arcosa Inc. by CRH plc.

daedf173a6:9a3df0112e45223a.title: Owner of Construction Company Sentenced to Prison for Obstructing IRS Efforts to Collect $1.4M in Unpaid Taxes
daedf173a6:9a3df0112e45223a.summary: The owner of a Texas construction company was sentenced today to 30 months in prison for obstructing the IRS’s efforts to collect unpaid employment taxes on behalf of the business he owned and operated.

daedf173a6:c05af1815ddf22c8.title: Syrian Man Sentenced for Wide-Ranging Hacking Conspiracy Conducted on Behalf of the Bashar Al Assad Regime
daedf173a6:c05af1815ddf22c8.summary: Today a federal district court in the Eastern District of Virginia sentenced Ahmad Umar Agha to 42 months in prison for his central role in an expansive hacking conspiracy organized and led by members of former Syrian President Bashar Al-Assad’s inner circle, including the commander of Syria’s General Intelligence Directorate, from as early as Aug. 24, 2011, to Jan. 31, 2024.

daedf173a6:5aec74aedaccdc66.title: Cuban Nationals and Florida Man Sentenced for Their Roles in an International Alien Smuggling, Asylum Fraud, and Money Laundering Conspiracy
daedf173a6:5aec74aedaccdc66.summary: Five Cuban nationals and one U.S. citizen were sentenced today for their roles in a vast conspiracy involving alien smuggling, asylum fraud, and money laundering.

daedf173a6:2df970d330201ed4.title: Chinese National Sentenced to 12 Years in Prison for Narcotics Trafficking, Money Laundering, and Material Support to Terrorism
daedf173a6:2df970d330201ed4.summary: Wenshen Xu, 52, a Honduras-based Chinese national extradited from Guatemala, was sentenced today to 12 years in prison, five years of supervised release, and a $22 million money judgement for conspiring to import cocaine into the United States, conspiring to launder money derived from drug trafficking, and to providing material support to a designated Foreign Terrorist Organization, specifically the Cartel de Jalisco Nueva Generacion (CJNG).

daedf173a6:083606d742085fef.title: Justice Department Releases Eighth Annual Elder Justice Report
daedf173a6:083606d742085fef.summary: Today, the Department of Justice’s Civil Division released its Annual Report to Congress on its efforts to Combat Elder Fraud and Abuse . The report summarizes the department’s extensive enforcement, victim support, training and myriad other efforts to promote elder justice during the reporting period from July 1, 2025, through June 30, 2026.

daedf173a6:c61632a0b4ed6aa2.title: Former Army Official Pleads Guilty to Conspiracy, Bribery, and Major Fraud Related to Hawaii Defense Contracts

daedf173a6:ea7d2b90c4d8a951.title: Ohio Man Convicted for Lying About His Involvement in the Rwandan Genocide
daedf173a6:ea7d2b90c4d8a951.summary: A federal jury convicted Eric Tabaro Nshimiye, also known as Eric Tabaro Nshimiyimana, 54, yesterday on four counts of perjury and one count of obstruction of justice related to his concealment of material information concerning his involvement in the 1994 Rwandan genocide.

daedf173a6:58f759396b48a25d.title: Court Orders Miami Tax Return Preparer to Permanently Shut Down Tax Preparation Business
daedf173a6:58f759396b48a25d.summary: The U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Florida issued a permanent injunction against Miami area tax return preparer Aniel Saint-Hilaire. The injunction bars Saint-Hilaire from acting as a return preparer, preparing tax returns or advising others in the preparation of tax returns, investing in or receiving fees from a tax return preparation business, or working in or consulting with a tax return preparation business.

daedf173a6:5b824df9065396e8.title: Virginia Mental Health Professional Charged in $49M Medicaid Fraud Scheme
daedf173a6:5b824df9065396e8.summary: A federal grand jury in the Eastern District of Virginia returned an indictment on Oct. 20 against Mikia Antoneice Noble, 37, of North Chesterfield, Virginia, for a $49 million mental health crisis services fraud scheme targeting Virginia Medicaid. Noble was arrested today.

ef78496c13:1b25c4cb38967f26.title: Taxing Capital to Protect It
ef78496c13:1b25c4cb38967f26.author: Ly, Hengrina
ef78496c13:1b25c4cb38967f26.summary: This paper studies the composition of taxation when the government cannot fully commit to respecting private returns after investment. A fiscal authority must finance a given expenditure from labor and capital income. Ordinary tax receipts are protected, but an opportunistic executive can seize part of the remaining capital payment. We show that a revenue-neutral increase in the capital tax raises the probability of compliance whenever the labor tax is below its local, fixedwage revenue peak, provided the equilibrium remains on a regular mixing branch. This result does not depend on the elasticity of substitution between capital and labor. The same reform can raise investment: the gain in expected retention must outweigh the decline in the opportunist’s continuation gain as compliance becomes less informative. We also characterize the Ramsey allocation conditional on full compliance. Limited commitment then imposes a ceiling on sustainable capital payments, rather than a general lower bound on the statutory capital-tax rate. Finally, we distinguish a change in the authority’s concern for the future from an increase in both actors’ patience. The former favors more informative policies when continuation welfare is convex; the latter has no unconditional direction in the reduced-form policy problem.

ef78496c13:2a829ab142f8603a.title: AI subsidies as a tool for redistribution
ef78496c13:2a829ab142f8603a.author: Lucas Parmentier
ef78496c13:2a829ab142f8603a.summary: I study the optimal taxation of artificial intelligence (AI). My analysis highlights a wage-compression effect that provides a rationale for subsidizing AI, as AI adoption may reduce rather than increase wage inequality. When this effect outweighs AI's social costs, AI should be subsidized instead of taxed. I treat AI as a productive input distinct from robots, as the two technologies perform different ranges of tasks. Using numerical simulations, I demonstrate that the optimal policy for AI may differ sharply from that for robots. Under the benchmark calibration, AI is subsidized, whereas robots are taxed. Therefore, the case for taxing AI is weaker than is commonly assumed. When AI lowers the skill premium, fiscal policy may need to encourage, rather than slow, adoption.

ef78496c13:d25c012959c8c987.title: Perverse Tax Incentives and the Destruction of Creative Works
ef78496c13:d25c012959c8c987.author: Maher, Luke
ef78496c13:d25c012959c8c987.summary: In late 2023, Warner Bros. Discovery announced that it would be permanently shelving Coyote vs. Acme, a complete and hotly anticipated film about popular Looney Tunes characters. This announcement was widely understood—and admitted by Warner Bros. Discovery in its Securities and Exchange Commission filings—to be motivated, at least in part, by a desire to “write off” the film’s costs for tax purposes. This Article is the first to (1) provide a full account for the tax rules that govern what constitutes a “loss” for purposes of unreleased creative works, (2) evaluate whether those rules make sense from both a technical and policy perspective (concluding that they do not), and (3) compare the relative merit of other approaches to allowing tax losses for unreleased creative works. In so doing, this Article makes two necessary contributions to current tax scholarship: first, it links the robust property scholarship on waste to tax policy, setting forth a framework through which critical reappraisals of long-entrenched tax laws and policies can be conducted, identifying ossified policies that no longer comport with our policy goals and revenue-raising needs and developing ways to improve them. Second, it also offers guidance in the ways that the law can think about the ownership, abandonment, and taxation of intangible assets.

ef78496c13:3bb778580565e14b.title: Implicit Pension Taxes over the Life Cycle: Efficiency Costs and Tax Smoothing
ef78496c13:3bb778580565e14b.author: Lundberg, Jacob
ef78496c13:3bb778580565e14b.summary: This paper studies the efficiency cost of pay-as-you-go pension systems. The return on pension contributions – typically average income growth – is lower than the market return on capital. Because the gap between these returns compounds over the life cycle, early-career contributions have a higher implicit tax rate. I develop a sufficient-statistics framework in which the deadweight loss depends on the age profile of implicit tax rates. Deadweight loss is minimized when the implicit tax rate is constant, mirroring the logic of tax smoothing. I then propose an implementation within a notional defined contribution design: contributions are valorized at a higher, market-based rate of return, while a lower fraction of contributions is credited to notional accounts and the remainder treated as a pure tax. Finally, I apply my deadweight loss formula to OECD PAYGO pension systems. Under the assumed parameter values, the deadweight loss averages 19 percent. I find that only 0.2 percentage points is attributable to the uneven timing of implicit taxation.

ef78496c13:5fda887cad01a0f8.title: The Net Present Value of the California Billionaire Tax Act
ef78496c13:5fda887cad01a0f8.author: Joshua Rauh
ef78496c13:5fda887cad01a0f8.summary: This paper examines the revenue and migration impact of the 2026 California Billionaire Tax Act, a one-time 5 percent tax on the worldwide net worth of individuals exceeding $1 billion. Using data from the Forbes Billionaire List, news reports detailing the residential real estate holdings of California billionaires, and public announcements of billionaire departures from the state, we estimate the behavioral response and associated revenue loss to this new tax using several different methodologies. Even before accounting for reductions in other tax bases such as the income tax, we estimate that the Act will collect approximately $30 billion (range $28 to 36 billion), less than a third of the $100 billion projected by Galle et al. (2025). This range accounts for the publicly confirmed taxpayer migration that has already eliminated nearly 30 percent of the Act's wealth tax base, applies a litigation-survival discount to the remaining base, and is validated by the wealth tax base elasticity literature. We estimate that California's billionaires contribute $3.3–5.8 billion annually in state income taxes. The present value of permanently lost income tax collections from departures more than offsets the one-time wealth tax revenue, yielding a net present value of negative $38.9 billion. Across 100, 000 simulated revenue and discount rate combinations, 85 percent of plausible outcomes produce a negative net present value of state revenues.

ef78496c13:a8cff203e584ffa1.title: Greed versus Fear: Optimal Time-Consistent Taxation with Default
ef78496c13:a8cff203e584ffa1.author: Vytautas Valaitis
ef78496c13:a8cff203e584ffa1.summary: This paper studies optimal time-consistent distortionary taxation with default. The government taxes labor income or issues non-contingent debt to finance an exogenous stochastic stream of fiscal shocks. Debt can be repudiated subject to default costs. Optimal policy is characterized by two opposing incentives that capture the double lack of commitment to old tax policies and to repaying debt, respectively: an incentive to postpone taxes by issuing more debt for the future (â€œGreedâ€ ), and an incentive to tax more currently to avoid punishing default premia (â€œFearâ€ ). A Generalized Euler Equation captures these forces and determines the optimal back-loading or front-loading of tax distortions. Even with small default risk, tax-smoothing and debt issuance are substantially limited when short-term debt is available. The same mechanisms operate in environments with long-term debt, but debt serves more as a fiscal absorber.

ef78496c13:dd6e53e0c11b6771.title: When Should Robots Be Subsidized?
ef78496c13:dd6e53e0c11b6771.author: Klaus Prettner
ef78496c13:dd6e53e0c11b6771.summary: This paper studies optimal robot taxation in a static model with routine and non-routine workers. Robots substitute for routine workers and complement non-routine workers. In addition, robots are produced in a monopolistic sector that charges a markup over marginal cost. In the absence of monopoly power, the optimal robot tax rate is zero. When robot producers have monopoly power, the optimal policy corrects the markup distortion by aligning the effective robot price with marginal cost, conditional on the labor supply induced by the income tax system. The wage premium rises with the expansion of the tasks that robots can perform and declines with higher robot production costs. The results clarify the conditions under which robot taxation serves as a corrective instrument.

ef78496c13:0450f280498fb7ba.title: State Child Tax Credits and Parental Labor Supply: Evidence from Staggered Adoption
ef78496c13:0450f280498fb7ba.author: Parolin, Zachary
ef78496c13:0450f280498fb7ba.summary: States increasingly supplement the federal Child Tax Credit (CTC) with credits that vary in generosity, refundability, and earnings requirements. We examine changes in parental employment, labor force participation, and work hours following state CTC adoption using the Current Population Survey Annual Social and Economic Supplement (CPS-ASEC), 2004–2026. Our preferred stacked difference-in-differences design includes 12 adopting states with complete event-time support and compares them with never-treated states and states that adopted after our evaluation window. Averaging over the first three post-adoption survey years, the estimated effect is 0.05 percentage points (SE 1.03) for employment and −0.46 points (0.82) for labor force participation; estimates for work hours are also close to zero. Across secondary specifications and CPS Basic Monthly analyses, extensive-margin estimates were similarly small. Larger simulated benefits are associated with fewer hours among employed parents, but the relationship is also evident before adoption and may partly reflect how benefits depend on earnings. Overall, the estimates provide little indication that state CTC adoption has substantially reduced parental employment, although meaningful effects in either direction cannot be ruled out under moderate departures from parallel trends.

ef78496c13:69562ce07e17f2f8.title: Taxing top wealth: migration responses and their aggregate economic implications
ef78496c13:69562ce07e17f2f8.author: Munoz, Mathilde
ef78496c13:69562ce07e17f2f8.summary: Using administrative data from Scandinavian countries, we provide evidence on international migration responses to wealth taxes and evaluate their aggregate economic implications. We find significant migration responses among the wealthy: a 1pp increase in the top wealth tax rate decreases the stock of wealthy taxpayers by about 2%. A large fraction of the wealthy are business owners, and their businesses are negatively affected by owner out-migration. The aggregate effects are nevertheless modest: the migration responses to a 1pp increase in the top wealth tax rate reduce employment by 0.02%, investments by 0.07%, and value-added by 0.10%.

ef78496c13:5c102bc5df1c8bb3.title: Fiscal integration as a Pareto improvement
ef78496c13:5c102bc5df1c8bb3.author: Bonfanti, Giovanni
ef78496c13:5c102bc5df1c8bb3.summary: Fiscal integration in a currency union is generally understood as a transfer from fiscally strong to fiscally weak countries. I show that this changes when common debt is paired with a non-defaultable common tax, even if national debt remains defaultable. The risky country gains from intertemporal trade: it receives a grant financed by a perpetual obligation it discounts more heavily than lenders do. The cost to the safe member is second-order and the tax removes it by insuring imperfectly correlated cycles rather than transferring resources in expectation. The calibration delivers a narrow Pareto-improving region: the tax that eliminates the risky country’s perverse incentive to default is negligible, while the tax that compensates the safe country is an order of magnitude larger. Joint spending on a public good expands the region and reverses that ordering: the safe country gains even before the common budget balances. JEL Classification: F34, F36, F45, H63, H87

ef78496c13:eca2edd3a3e68962.title: Illustrating long-run fiscal challenges using the Long-Term Model
ef78496c13:eca2edd3a3e68962.author: Yvan Guillemette
ef78496c13:eca2edd3a3e68962.summary: This paper presents updated estimates of long-run fiscal gaps for 35 OECD and accession candidate countries using the OECD Global Long-Term Model. The long-run fiscal gap measures the fiscal adjustment required at the 2060 horizon to keep public debt ratios stable near current levels while maintaining current service standards and benefit entitlements. The methodology incorporates several refinements, including projected increases in defence spending and a more detailed treatment of primary expenditure. In the absence of additional policy action, the median country would require a fiscal adjustment of 4.7 percentage points of GDP between 2027 and 2060 to stabilise debt, with substantially larger adjustments in some countries. Population ageing is the main driver of long-run fiscal pressures through higher pension, health and long-term care spending, compounded in many cases by weak initial fiscal positions. The paper also assesses the sensitivity of fiscal gaps to key assumptions and policy scenarios.

ef78496c13:5149234641e39737.title: Puff, Puff, Tax: Internal Revenue Code Section 280E Penalizes State-Sanctioned Marijuana Companies and Undermines the Ability-To-Pay Principle
ef78496c13:5149234641e39737.author: Thomas, Joseph E.
ef78496c13:5149234641e39737.summary: This Comment argues that Internal Revenue Code § 280E unfairly penalizes state-licensed marijuana businesses by denying ordinary business deductions and taxing them on amounts that may exceed their actual profits. Examining the history of § 280E and recent challenges by marijuana dispensaries, the Comment contends that the provision undermines the ability-to-pay principle and threatens the viability of legitimate cannabis businesses operating under state law. It concludes that Congress should amend or repeal § 280E as applied to state-sanctioned marijuana companies. [This abstract was written by Microsoft Copilot, a generative artificial intelligence.]

ef78496c13:ff7c9e7ffc66d431.title: HORIZONTAL INEQUALITY IN OPTIMALTAXATION: EVIDENCE FROM A DEVELOPMENT CONTEXT
ef78496c13:ff7c9e7ffc66d431.author: Magnus Eldrup
ef78496c13:ff7c9e7ffc66d431.summary: Exemptions are a key feature of income tax systems in developing countries, yet standard optimal tax models cannot explain them. By assuming full compliance, these models ignore horizontal inequality between formal and informal workers, understating the social cost of taxing the former. Extending the optimal tax framework, I incorporate informality and horizontal inequality aversion. I conduct a survey experiment in Kenya, finding that respondents place substantially higher welfare weight on formal taxpayers than otherwise identical informal workers. Combining these empirical preferences with administrative tax data yields prescriptions of high exemption thresholds matching observed policy, a result alternative explanations cannot rationalize.

ef78496c13:07a32f71b5767c53.title: Inheritance Taxation and the Allocation of Productive Assets in Family Firms
ef78496c13:07a32f71b5767c53.author: Roedriguez del Valle, Adrian
ef78496c13:07a32f71b5767c53.summary: We examine how taxation of intergenerational transfers affects the allocation of productive assets within family firms. Using administrative registry data on family-farm successions in Sweden around the 2005 abolition of inheritance and gift taxes, we investigate how the successor’s share of land holdings in the parental and sibling generations responds to the removal of taxes. We use a quasi-experimental event-study design and find that the increase in the successor’s ownership share is about 10–11 percentage points larger among families with greater predetermined exposure to the pre-reform inheritance tax. Results also indicate that the reform led parents to transfer assets earlier and concentrate a larger share of productive assets in the successor through inter vivos gifts. Post-reform successions are associated with higher capital intensity, suggesting that inheritance and gift taxation extends beyond the direct tax burden, affecting property-right allocation and capital intensity in family-operated enterprises.

I did mention in the course of the post that I have no interest in selling my estimate of value to the rest of the world, both because I don't own the high ground here and because it is meant to guide my decisions, not yours. That is why I made my model open to changes that you can make to my story and inputs, and while you have to trust my mechanics, I tried to carry your inputs into value. Much of the pushback I have received has been thoughtful and productive, some of it has been emotional (either from people who love Anthropic or from those who would not touch it with a ten-foot pole) and some of it, especially on the cost of capital, reflects a fundamental disconnect with market history, current market pricing and just basic business sense. I plan to play devil's advocate with my own valuation, looking at my story inputs, and ranking them in order of fragility, partly to stress-test my value estimate and partly to reinforce some corporate finance first principles, and then move on to your feedback and what I take away from it. I tried to value SpaceX ahead of and after the filing of the prospectus for its initial public offering before moving on to the question of whether it and OpenAI and Anthropic should be part of the S&P 500 index . I started my analysis of how AI would affect the rest of us , from doomsday to do-nothing scenarios, largely in response to Citrini and Citadel reports on the topic. in August 2026, I took my first big picture look at AI as a business, which I titled its bar mitzvah moment, with a look at its potential market, business economics and moats. That look was a prelude to the initial public offerings in the works (then) for Anthropic and OpenAI, and I provided a simple way to reverse engineer how much investors would need in revenues from these companies to justify their sky-high pricing. In early October, I looked at how the massive investments in AI are playing out in the aggregate earnings , cashflows and invested capital at US companies, and why it is contributing to holding the market intact, in the face of rising rates. Just last week, I argued that both Anthropic and OpenAI would be priced , rather than valued, for their initial public offerings, using what I called buzzy metrics (like annualized run rates) and promised that I would try to value the company, when it filed its prospectus. On October 26, Anthropic filed its prospectus , and at the risk of being called hopelessly wrong by both bulls and bears, I will try to value the company, using what I see as its most likely pathway, while also leaving the door open for you to disagree with me, and pick your own pathways to valuing the company. b0a91b96f4:7ec112c975bad06e.title: From Eyeballs to Annual Run Rates (ARR): Buzzy Pricing Metrics and the Anthropic Trade!
b0a91b96f4:7ec112c975bad06e.author: Aswath Damodaran (noreply@blogger.com)
b0a91b96f4:7ec112c975bad06e.summary: I was in San Francisco last week to talk to NYU Stern Alumni on October 15, and it was the day that Anthropic had a pre-IPO meeting with prospective investors. While I was not at the meeting, the focus of teh gathering was laying a foundation for its upcoming IPO, with the company reporting third-quarter revenue of $16.8 billion, which news reports described as surging 45% over the previous quarter's revenues, and positive profits, albeit on an adjusted basis. During the meeting, Anthropic also reported an annual revenue run rate (ARR) of $67 billion, a metric that those in the AI space have adopted with gusto, with an estimate that the ARR would exceed $100 billion by the end of the year. The nature of ARR, where choices on how revenue is calculated (gross versus net) and on annualization periods (daily, weekly or monthly) can make a significant difference, has led investors to be skeptical about comparing these numbers across time and companies. While I share some of that skepticism, it is worth remembering that young businesses are often priced on inventive metrics, some with more basis than others. In the late nineties, dot.com companies were priced not just on the number of visitors to their websites, but on eyeballs , where Mary Meeker argued that ad spending at these companies was correlated with time that these visitors spent on websites (eyeballs) rather than total visitors. In the last decade, you saw social media companies priced based upon the number of users and subscription-based companies on subscriber numbers. In this post, I will try to lay out the rationale for why pricing supplants valuation in young companies and why that pricing almost always has to be built around messy metrics like eyeballs, users and ARR, rather than more conventional metrics like earnings, book value or cash flows. The second is US debt exceeding $40 trillion for the first time , bringing attention to a long-standing worry that this debt burden may be hitting a tipping point for bond buyers. The third is a that the Federal Reserve has a new chair in Kevin Warsh, and for the many Fed Watchers, who are uncertain about where he plans to lead the Fed, the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting coming up in mid-September looms larger than ever. In this post, I hope to step back from the day-to-day coverage of US treasury yields and look at their performance in 2026, not only with a longer term perspective, but also in the context of movements in long terms yields in government bonds in other currencies. I also intend to revisit a discussion that I initiated in 2022, when interest rates were the central act in markets, about the relationship between interest rates and stock prices, and why higher rates do not always translate into lower stock prices, and why that effect will vary across sectors and companies. Government Borrowing Rates Governments borrow money and often do so by issuing bonds in financial markets. The rates on these bonds reflect the concerns that lenders have about the purchasing power of the currencies that they are issued in, and government bond rates, for better or worse, become indicators that drive day-to-day market movements in almost all asset classes. In this section, I will begin with an examination of US treasury rates before expanding the discussion to government bond rates in other currencies. 1aa97d921e:bd2718ce7fe44e03.title: Anti-Monopoly as Industrial Policy: The Chicago School Versus Adam Smith
1aa97d921e:bd2718ce7fe44e03.author: Richard R. John
1aa97d921e:bd2718ce7fe44e03.summary: Jolted by the Great Depression of the 1930s, Thurman Arnold devised an anti-monopoly industrial policy for the United States Justice Department that breathed fresh life into a then-moribund Sherman Anti-Trust Act. Arnold’s jurisprudence built on Adam Smith’s discovery that market-making could promote national security and forestall civil unrest. Smith’s insights had informed the industrial policy of Alexander Hamilton, who laid the groundwork in the 1790s for the country’s economic development. Edward H. Levi brought Arnold’s pragmatic anti-monopolism to the University of Chicago. Here, ironically, Arnoldian jurisprudence would be transmogrified into the doctrinaire company-over-country market fundamentalism of the Chicago School of Economics. Today, writes Richard R. John, as we envision for the 21st century a new pro-market, pro-freedom, pro-national security industrial policy, it is worth recalling how U. S. economic development took the form that it did, why the Chicago School repudiated the enduring wisdom of Adam Smith, and what this portends for the world of today. Read it at ProMarket >>

1aa97d921e:1bc106d2fe57d9bb.title: How George Stigler and the Chicago School Opened the Marketplace of Ideas to Business

1aa97d921e:93e02838a27ed28b.title: The Chicago School Abandoned the Positive Freedom of Adam Smith and the Founding Fathers
1aa97d921e:93e02838a27ed28b.author: Maha Rafi Atal
1aa97d921e:93e02838a27ed28b.summary: Adam Smith’s theory of political economy did not begin with the isolated individual but rather the individual who operates to earn the respect of others. In the 1970s and ‘80s, the Chicago School abandoned this aspect of freedom in preference of the isolated individual, which in turn produced a weaker concept of freedom, morality, and society that has stifled the cultivation of all three in the United States, writes Maha Rafi Atal. 1aa97d921e:8cf8fcb20f958484.title: Adam Smith’s Moral Philosophy Complicates Interpretations by the Chicago School and Its Critics
1aa97d921e:8cf8fcb20f958484.author: Sandra Peart and David Levy
1aa97d921e:8cf8fcb20f958484.summary: The connections between Adam Smith’s Wealth of Nations and Theory of Moral Sentiments reveal a much more complicated understanding of how markets work than developed in the common interpretation by the Chicago School of economics or that of its critics. 1aa97d921e:f1e2511bf4ba4c0f.title: America Became Rich Because of Liberalism
